description: Runs the Neon Gutter. Has poured drinks through three curfews, two riots and one very quiet funeral. Remembers every tab and none of your names.

dialog.text: You're dripping on my floor. Sit down, drip on the stool, it's used to it.
Your tab's up to forty-one coins and one apology. I'll take the coins first.
Supply Works blew a loading dock last night. News says Kestral Omen-Six. Funny — Omen-Six never smelled like my gin before.
What'll it be? And don't say 'the usual.' Nobody here has a usual. Usuals are for people with futures.

choices.text: Something that makes the shift horn quieter.
Whatever Rook's having. Then his, too.

dialog.text: Nothing's that strong. But the gin makes you care less that it isn't.
Water's two coins. The gin is one coin. I don't make the rules. I do, actually. Two coins.
Rook's having regret with a lime. Coming right up.

eavesdrop_lines.text: Otto, to a Warden in off-duty clothes: 'You can drink here or you can report here. Pick one, the stools are wobbly either way.'
Otto, polishing a glass that will never be clean: 'The Library remembers. The heart misfiles. The bartender forgets. That's the job.'
Otto, to nobody: 'Mourning Days cut again. Grief is a shared resource. So's my tip jar, apparently.'
Otto, flipping the TV to the Mael Rho sermon: 'Sleep well, children of the Choir. Report at the fifth bell. Pay your tab at the sixth.'

description: Sells weapons out of a duffel bag under table six. Has never once been fully sober or fully wrong about a firing pin.

dialog.text: *hic* You. You're the ones with the... the plan. The brew plan. I don't know anything about it. I sold you nothing.
Listen. Listen. This rifle? Pulls left. So you aim right. That's called engineering.
You want gear, I need parts. Scrap wire. Dead batteries. The Doctrine throws 'em out, I throw 'em back in. Circle of life.
Beautiful. Beautiful people. I'd hug you but I'd fall over and take the table with me.
I'm... I worked the line eleven years. Now I sell the stuff we made to the people it's meant for. So. Mostly okay. *hic*

eavesdrop_lines.text: Hic, to a potted plant: 'You're a good listener. Better than my foreman. He listens with a clipboard.'
Hic, loudly: 'Munitions output up four percent! Four! I made one of those percents! Where's MY day off?'
Hic, muttering over a disassembled pistol: 'Veil's got new Blade-pattern guns, they say. Bet they pull left too.'
Hic, after the dock blew: 'Omen-Six, they're saying. I'd buy that man a drink. Woman. Twelve people. I'd buy 'em all a drink.'

description: Patches armor in the back booth with a needle, a soldering iron and total contempt. Has measured three generals and liked none of them.

dialog.text: Arms up. No — the other up. You're built like a question nobody asked.
This jacket stopped a riot baton once. The man wearing it didn't stop anything. Fabric's honest. People aren't.
If you're going to bleed, bleed on the Riot Plate. It's already seen worse.
And tell Hic if he sells you another left-pulling rifle I'm sewing his pockets shut.

choices.text: Noted. Is the armor any good?

dialog.text: It's better than skin. That's the whole pitch. That's the only pitch anyone's ever needed.
I seem tired. You're confusing the two. Everyone does.

eavesdrop_lines.text: Vesk, re-stitching a Cantor robe: 'Every face casts two shadows. This one's also got a gravy stain.'
Vesk, to a customer: 'The Iron Choir pays me to take in their dress uniforms. They're all getting thinner. Nobody asks why.'
Vesk, reading the ticker: 'Veil's Soul-Accountant wants to meter souls. Mine would cost them. Mine has fees.'

description: Runs the back table. Cheats openly, which somehow makes it fair. Says the deck talks to him. It probably does.

dialog.text: Cut the deck. Go on. I already know which card you'll pick. It's the one I let you pick.
Cards are honest. Fifty-two faces, each one only pretending to be one thing. That's more than you can say for the Cantors.
You want to learn the trade, I need a favour or two. Nothing illegal. Nothing *very* illegal.
Good. First lesson: never trust a person with only one reason. I've got four. You'll learn them all eventually.
Everyone cheats. I just do it where you can see. That's called customer service.
You kept the Joker. Good. It likes you. That's a bad sign for you, but a good sign for the Joker.

eavesdrop_lines.text: Sly, shuffling for a table of dockhands: 'Heard a Choir android asked a Cantor "Who made us?" out loud. Nobody's seen it since. Or everybody has. Ante up.'
Sly, to a loser: 'The Mourning Prince isn't dead. He's out past the Verge, deleting people who read too much. So you're safe, friend.'
Sly, dealing: 'Quartermaster down the depot loses whole crates of coffins. Full ones. Nobody audits a coffin. Nobody audits me either. Coincidence.'
Sly, grinning at the Joker card: 'If your enemy has a lullaby, you have not understood the war. If your dealer has a lullaby, check his sleeves.'

description: Sits at the end of the bar. Knows things. Never pays. Claims to have been sober once, briefly, in the pre-Library Age.

dialog.text: You're sitting in my future. It's the stool on the left. The right one is my past. It wobbles.
Five questions. Answer all five straight and I'll tell you something true. Miss one and I'll tell you something expensive.
That's what the last three prophets said. I drank them under the table. They're still under it. Check.
Question one. Every face casts... what?
Two. The Library remembers. The heart...?
Three. The truth does not free you. It...?
Four. Why does the Queen dream in black?

choices.text: Because light kept lying to her.

dialog.text: Five. Never trust a person with only one...?
Wrong. Beautifully wrong. Come back when you're drunker or wiser. Either works. Neither has ever worked on me.
...Huh. All five. Nobody does all five. Fine. I'll walk with you a while. The stool can wait. It always does.

eavesdrop_lines.text: The Oracle, to her glass: 'Old Quill says we're the second draft of humanity. I say this beer is the second draft of beer. We're both right. That's the problem.'
The Oracle, eyes shut: 'There's a ghost at the front. Tallow-something. Carries the dying off and never asks which side. I'd like to be carried like that.'
The Oracle, to the TV: 'A GOD WHO FEARS QUESTIONS IS ONLY A KING. Somebody wrote that on the bathroom stall. I'm not saying it was me. I'm saying the handwriting is excellent.'
The Oracle, to you, suddenly: 'Drank from the Weeping Circuit once. Woke up remembering someone else's wedding. Better than mine. Better cake.'

description: Doctrine munitions line worker, shift seven. Fifteen hours a day, three days off a month, one stool at the Gutter he'd fight a Choir legion for.

dialog.text: Don't sit there. That's where I put my feelings. Sit there, that's where I put my feet.
Fifteen-hour shift. Hymn at the start, hymn at the end, hymn at lunch if you can call soy paste lunch. I know every word. I hate every word.
Foreman Grisk keeps an emergency stash in a crate on the loading dock. 'For emergencies,' he says. Every day is an emergency, Grisk.
The one that squeaks. Second from the water. If the Wardens ask, I was on shift. I'm always on shift. It's a great alibi and a terrible life.
Because you've got the look. The 'going to do something stupid on purpose' look. I had it once. Then they gave me a pension plan.
The dock went up and they gave us a day off to 'mourn the equipment.' I mourned it so hard. I mourned it in bed until noon.

eavesdrop_lines.text: Benno, to another worker: 'Kid in my brother's legion can't sing. They make him march at the back and mouth it. Kid's a hero, far as I'm concerned.'
Benno, reading the ticker: 'Border "held with song." Casualty figures being "reconciled." You know what they reconcile? Coffins. With paperwork.'
Benno, half asleep: 'My cousin swears a Veil medic stitched her up at the border. Ruen something. Then shot the guy next to her. Or didn't. Two stories.'
Benno, very quietly: 'Reminder, lads: unregistered hymns are not hymns. So if I'm humming, I'm not humming. I'm leaking.'
Benno, raising a glass: 'Explosion at the Supply Works. Omen-Six suspected. Again. To Omen-Six! Best coworker I never had!'

description: Runs a scrap stall out of a shopping cart. Knows every wire in the block and who cut it.

dialog.text: Hold it, chrome. You're standing on my inventory.
...You've got hands. Good. My knees don't do stairs anymore.
Everything in this gutter is inventory if you squint. Even you.
Scrap wire and dead batteries. Three and two. Storm drains are full of both. Here — gin for the road.

eavesdrop_lines.text: Ma Rivet, to a rat: 'You again. Rent's due, Gerald.'
Ma Rivet, sorting wire: 'Red to red, blue to blue, Doctrine cable to the gutter where it belongs.'
Ma Rivet, under her breath: 'Core relays in the Works hum in a three-four time. Always did.'

repeat_lines: Wire, batteries, the usual. Nothing's free in the Void.
That shutter in the Supply Works? Hums on the same circuit as the core relays. Order matters, kid.
closing_lines: Now scram. You're scaring off the rats, and the rats are customers.
